This is the same guy who was pushing QuidelOrtho ($QDEL) shortly after COVID, calling it his #1 stock pick. Look at how that turned out. Making money in the market doesn’t automatically make you a great stock picker, and a successful track record doesn’t mean every subsequent call deserves your trust. There’s a big difference between having made money in the past and having a repeatable investment process. Before following someone’s picks, look at their entire track record-the winners, the losers, and the calls they’d rather you forget. Anyone can look like a genius when you only hear about their winners. Cathie Wood is another perfect example. ARKK has struggled to keep up with the S&P 500, let alone beat it consistently. You can have a compelling story about disruptive innovation, make bold predictions about the future, and still deliver terrible returns for investors.
The market doesn’t reward conviction, a good narrative, or being right about a technology. It rewards buying good businesses at the right price and delivering returns over time.
Being right about the future means very little if your investors lose out on the returns they could have earned simply by owning the S&P 500.
